hint.text: The colour of human skin is determined by a natural colouring called melanin. The more melanin your skin contains, the darker its colour.
hint.label: Did you know?

atoms.b: Our skin allows us to explore our surroundings through ((++touch smell)). Thanks to receptors in our ((++skin nose)), we can sense when something comes into contact with our bodies.
Skin is the stretchy outer layer that covers and protects our bodies. With an average total area of around 2<mat>m^2</mat>, it’s the ((++largest smallest)) and heaviest organ in the human body!
Skin is made up of three layers. The uppermost layer is known as the ((++epidermis outskin)). This is the layer we can see on the outside of our bodies. Our ((++hairs joints)) grow out of this layer.

end.text: A human being has around five million hairs on their body – almost as many as a great ape! However, human hairs are much finer.

atoms.b: If you take a close look at the epidermis, you can also see pores, which are small openings that release ((++sweat tears)). This process is used to ((++cool warm)) the body.

Under the epidermis, you can find the dermis. This layer contains the receptors that send information to the ((++brain ear)) via the nervous system. This allows us to sense stimuli such as warmth, ((++cold brightness)), pressure, pain and ((++contact sound)).

The lowest layer of the skin is the fatty tissue. It is made up tissue, which protects the organs below, and ((++fat_cells nails)), which keep the body warm. The fatty tissue also contains a network of nerves and blood vessels.

What can we feel using the receptors in our skin? Match up the words and pictures.
